groups.title: Antispasmodic Analgesic Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for paroxysmal pain of gastrointestinal disease and for functional disorders and spasmodic pain of the biliary and urinary systems.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 to 2 tablets 3 times a day. Do not exceed a maximum of 6 tablets a day.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Spasmodic pain of the gastrointestinal, biliary and urinary systems
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Maximum 6 tablets a day; regular alcohol use

groups.title: Antihistamine Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for allergic rhinitis and chronic idiopathic urticaria.
groups.usage: For adults and children aged 12 years and over, 1 capsule once a day. Children aged 6 to under 12 years weighing 30 kg or more take 1 capsule once a day.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, are a child under 6 years, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or have galactose intolerance and related genetic problems. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Allergic rhinitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 6 years; pregnancy, breastfeeding; galactose intolerance

groups.title: Vitamin Supplement Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for physical fatigue, and during pregnancy and breastfeeding and during or after illness when strength is reduced.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 capsule once a day.
groups.caution: Taking 5000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause congenital malformation. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Physical fatigue; reduced strength in pregnancy, breastfeeding and illness
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Vitamin A above 5000 IU a day in pregnancy

groups.title: Children's Ibuprofen Syrup
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to reduce fever caused by acute upper respiratory tract infection.
groups.usage: For children aged 6 months and over, 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) per dose, every 4 to 6 hours as needed, not exceeding 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day. Refer to the approved product information for the recommended amount by age group.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Fever from acute upper respiratory tract infection in children
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 6 months; maximum 4 doses a day

groups.title: Vitamin Supplement Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used during pregnancy and breastfeeding and during or after illness when strength is reduced.
groups.usage: For people aged 8 years and over and adults, 1 tablet 2 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, are an infant under 3 months, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Reduced strength in pregnancy, breastfeeding and illness
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 3 months; galactose intolerance

groups.title: Ibuprofen Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for fever and pain caused by a cold, low back pain, period pain, rheumatoid arthritis and related joint conditions.
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout or psoriatic arthritis, adults take 1/2 capsule to 1.5 capsules (200 to 600 mg) 3 to 4 times a day, up to a maximum of 8 capsules (3200 mg) a day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight a day in 3 to 4 divided doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults take 1/2 capsule to 1 capsule (200 to 400 mg) 3 to 4 times a day. For migraine, adults start with 1/2 capsule.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Arthritis, fever and pain, period pain, migraine
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Maximum 3200 mg a day; gastrointestinal bleeding

groups.title: Expectorant Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for phlegm and for a cough caused by phlegm.
groups.usage: For adults and children aged 15 years and over, 2 capsules per dose; for children aged 8 to 14 years, 1 capsule per dose, 3 times a day after meals.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, have a gastric or duodenal ulcer, or are a child under 8 years. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Phlegm and cough caused by phlegm
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 8 years; gastric or duodenal ulcer

groups.title: Analgesic Antipyretic Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief in headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain and neuralgia.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over, 1 tablet per dose; for people aged 8 years to under 15 years, 1/2 tablet per dose, 3 times a day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Headache, toothache, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 8 years; at least 4 hours between doses

groups.title: Cold Relief Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain in a cold.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 2 capsules per dose; for people over 7 years to under 15 years, 1 capsule per dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Cold symptoms: sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, aches
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 7 years or under; regular alcohol use

groups.title: Vitamin E Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to supply vitamin E in older age and for peripheral circulatory disorder and shoulder and neck stiffness at the menopause.
groups.usage: For people aged 8 years and over and adults, 1 capsule 2 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine or to soybean oil, soya or peanut, are an infant under 12 months, or have a severe condition as stated in the approved information. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Vitamin E supply; peripheral circulatory disorder; menopausal stiffness
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 12 months; soya or peanut allergy

groups.title: Laxative Enteric-coated Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for constipation and for the loss of appetite, abdominal bloating and abnormal intestinal fermentation that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over, 1 to 2 tablets 3 times a day after meals. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses. Start with the smallest amount and increase or decrease it gradually while watching the shape and condition of the stool.
groups.caution: Do not take if you have an acute abdominal condition (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and similar) or intestinal obstruction. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Constipation and related bloating and poor appetite
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 15 years; acute abdominal disease; bowel obstruction

groups.title: Anti-inflammatory Analgesic Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used as supportive treatment for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylosing spondylitis and painful swelling or inflammation after trauma or surgery.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 capsule (300 mg) 2 to 4 times a day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) a day.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, pain and swelling after trauma or surgery
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Maximum 1200 mg a day; gastrointestinal bleeding

groups.title: Motion Sickness Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to prevent and relieve dizziness, vomiting and headache caused by motion sickness.
groups.usage: To prevent motion sickness, people aged 15 years and over take 1 tablet 30 minutes to 1 hour before travel. If symptoms appear, an additional single dose may be taken, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours, up to a limit of 3 doses a day.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are breastfeeding or are a child. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have experienced hypersensitivity to a medicine.

summaryTable.Use: Prevention and relief of motion sickness
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Children; breastfeeding; maximum 3 doses a day

groups.title: Cough and Phlegm Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for cough and phlegm.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 2 capsules 3 times a day after meals.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are an infant under 3 months. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Cough and phlegm
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 3 months; pregnancy

groups.title: Acid Reducer Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve heartburn associated with excess stomach acid.
groups.usage: For adults and people aged 15 years and over, 1 tablet per dose. Do not take more than 2 tablets within 24 hours.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine or to other H2 receptor antagonists, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Heartburn associated with excess stomach acid
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 15 years; galactose intolerance

groups.usage: For adults, 2 to 3 g a day in 2 to 3 divided doses. Adjust appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Carnitine deficiency; myocardial metabolic disorder
